Dear sons and successors in our **Art** <note>In this context, "the Art" refers to alchemy or the "Great Work" of spiritual and physical transformation.</note>, you should know that we hereby hand over to you this secret **Wisdom**, and we tell you by the highest truth, which is **God** Himself: if you do not apply this to the glory of **God**, if you let such things reach the wicked and the unrepentant, or if you are helpful to them with it, or use it for gruesome bloodshed, then believe for certain that the hand of the **Lord** will strike you in an instant. Nature: by day the sun, and by night the moon and stars. Included herewith are the writings of the famous **Toelten**, called **The Unlocked Heaven** <note>original: *Cœlum reseratum*</note>, which have never been printed because they were bought up while still in the press in Nuremberg. All the works from **minerals**, **metals**, **animals**, and **vegetables** are included, just as I have not only described the "chaotic" and "astral" works from the wondrous materials with all the practical maneuvers, and how to make the highest **tincture** <note>A potent alchemical substance used for transmutation or healing.</note> from each; but also how one should make pearls, **carbuncles** <note>term: *Carfunckel*; a historical name for any deep red gemstone, particularly garnets or rubies.</note>, diamonds, rubies, and all other stones, as good as and even better than those made by nature. ## Preface of Toeltius. <note>Johann Toeltius was the pseudonymous author of *Coelum Reseratum Chymicum* (The Chemical Heaven Unlocked), first published in the early 18th century.</note>

Dear Reader, I was not in the be-

present little work to go into
print; however, because ma-
ny have slandered my previous
little treatises, especially the *Chemical Light* <note>original: *Lumen Chymicum*</note>,
as if they were nothing but fantasies, with which
I sought something extraordinary from the world,
and thereby this noble art—which is nonetheless
truthful—is decried as the Devil’s delusion <term>delusion: *Blendwerck*, literally "blinding-work," referring to a deceptive trick or a demonic mirage</term>,

concerning this sort of people; for whatever such

has become a mere trade <term>trade: *Handthierung*, meaning a craft, business, or manual handling</term> to them,
which they have adopted according to their spirit-
less mind, so that they may lead the simple
away from the truth and toward their master, Lu-

gods by the simple,

<margin>Mercury of the Philosophers <note>original: "Mercurius Philosophorum"</note></margin>
To make the **Mercury of the Philosophers** <term>Mercurius Philosophorum</term> <note>A specialized alchemical solvent or "spirit" believed to be the essential soul of metals, not to be confused with common quicksilver.</note>: Take one pound of honest **raw antimony** <term>Antimonium crudum</term> <note>Naturally occurring antimony sulfide (stibnite).</note> and half a pound of **nitre** <term>Nitrum</term> <note>Saltpeter.</note>. Grind these well together and place them both into a glowing **crucible** <note>A ceramic or graphite container used for high-heat melting.</note> so that the nitre ignites and begins to flow. Take care that no coals fall into it, so that no **regulus** <term>Regulus</term> <note>A metallic mass or "button" that settles at the bottom of a crucible; here, the author wants to avoid isolating the metal too early.</note> precipitates, but rather that everything together becomes a single **slag** <note>The glassy byproduct of smelting.</note>. Then, take it from the fire, crush it small while it is still warm, and mix into it an equal weight of **sal ammoniac** <term>Salarmoniac</term> <note>Ammonium chloride, used as a flux and to aid sublimation.</note>. Put it into a **sublimation vessel** <term>Sublimatorium</term> and sublimate it. The Mercury of the Philosophers will then rise up with the **sublimate** <note>The solid product formed when a substance is heated to a vapor and then cools directly back into a solid.</note>. This is far better than the one mentioned in the previous chapter, for it flows over a light just like water. When this is mixed with a **gold-calx** <term>Gold-Kalck</term> <note>A powdered form of gold, usually an oxide.</note>, it yields one of the most powerful **tinctures** <note>In alchemy, a "tincture" is a substance capable of "dyeing" or transmuting a base metal into a noble one.</note> for transmuting mercury into gold, or with silver, for transmuting mercury into silver.

# Annotation.

Dear God, if all the writings of this author had likewise been shared with the world, how all the **mysteries** <term>Mysteria: secret or divine knowledge accessible only to the initiated</term> would have fallen into misuse! And although he kept many practical steps secret, he has nevertheless laid so much from Nature before the eyes of the world that nothing more is left from which it could have become uncommonly fortunate. Therefore, you students of our **brotherhood**, if you receive this into your hands, keep it sealed within you; it is better to die than to reveal such things to wicked boys.

Now, to come to this work and to describe it in detail:
<margin>
The **Fifth Essence** of minerals.
<note>original: *Quinta Essentia mineralium*</note>
</margin>
the **Fifth Essence** <term>Quint-Essenz: the most purified and potent form of a substance, believed to contain its medicinal or spiritual core</term> can be extracted from the minerals in a short time: the red of **antimony** <term>Antimonii: a semi-metal used in alchemy for its purifying properties</term>, the sky-blue of **bismuth**, the grass-green of **lead-ore**, as shall be described one by one, since the author leads us toward them. The author intends for one to pour the **extractions** together after the **putrefaction** <term>Putrefaction: the breakdown of matter through gentle heat to release its internal components</term>, and to place them in a cellar so that they might form **crystals**; however, this does not work in that way. Instead, half of the **solvent** <term>Menstruum: a powerful liquid used to dissolve solids or extract their essence</term> must be drawn off over a very gentle fire in a **water bath** <term>B. M.: abbreviation for *Balneum Mariae* (Mary's Bath), a double-boiler used to heat substances gently and evenly</term>, then that which is distilled—

# The Heavens Unlocked <note>original Latin: "Cœlum Referatum"</note>

## Note.

<margin>The Alcahest from Herbs <note>original Latin: "alcahest ex Herbis"</note></margin>
It is well to note, if one wishes to make the **<term>Alcahest: a hypothetical universal solvent sought by alchemists, capable of reducing any body to its primary matter</term>** from herbs, that one should first press them together into stone vessels and seal them tightly. Place the vessels in gentle warmth so that the herbs may thoroughly <term>putrefy: to undergo a process of biological decay or rotting</term>; for without true <term>putrefaction: the state of decomposition</term> nothing can be achieved, and it yields little "blood" <note>In alchemical terms, "blood" often refers to the deep red oils or the essential life-force extracted from a substance</note>. Even if they have stood for at least 6 months, they will still hardly be rightly decomposed; it is better if they stand for 9 months, for then the true putrefaction will have occurred.

### J. G. Töltius, Chapter 4.

<margin>Spirit, Body, Soul. Mercury, Salt, Sulfur.</margin>
<term>Phlegm</term> <note>original: "Phlegma"; a watery, inactive byproduct of distillation</note>, and whatever else wishes to pass over, some of the oil goes with it; and much <term>volatile salt</term> <note>original: "Salvolatile"; a crystalline substance that vaporizes easily, often smelling of ammonia</note> deposits itself; leave this in the **flask** <note>original: "Kolben"</note> and **helm** <note>original: "Helm"; the top part of a still</note>. **Rectify** <term>rectificire; to purify a liquid through repeated distillation</term> the **spirit** from its **phlegm**, along with the oil, and preserve it well; also keep the **phlegm**. ### J. G. Toeltius, Chapter 4

Distill by degrees as long as anything wishes to pass over; in this way, you will obtain a **vinegar** <note>original Latin: *Acetum*</note>. Rectify this from the **phlegm** <term>Phlegma</term> <note>The watery, inactive component of a liquid.</note> it still contains, and preserve it well. ## The First Composition.

<margin>The first composition for durable crucibles <note>original Latin: *Compositio Crucibulorum durabilium prima*</note>.</margin>
For this, the best clay is needed, both blue and white, of the kind that turns to stone when fired. Take a cartload of such clay; beat it and prepare it. Once it is separated from all stones, dry it and sift it through a sieve. When it is well-prepared, add finely crushed and burnt brick dust—though silica <note>original: *Kiesel*</note> is better—and also sifted hammer scale <term>the iron oxide flakes that fall off hot metal in a blacksmith's forge</term> and salt. Work these well together. The standard proportions are: take 6 pounds of clay, 1 pound of crushed silica, 1 pound of hammer scale, and two handfuls of salt. From this material, make crucibles <term>heat-resistant containers for melting metals</term> a good thumb’s thickness, as high and as large as you wish, and fire them. This material also serves for cupels <term>shallow porous cups used in assaying gold and silver</term>, scorifiers <term>shallow clay dishes used in smelting</term>, muffles <term>refractory enclosures to protect materials from direct flame</term>, flasks, and retorts. If you wish to glaze them, simply pour finely crushed Venetian glass and salt over them and fire.

# The Second Composition, which is the Best.

<margin>The second and best <note>original Latin: *Secunda et optima*</note>.</margin>
Take good clay and let it dry thoroughly in the sun, then sift four pounds of it through a hair-sieve. Take half a pound of crushed and burnt pebbles <note>likely flint or silica</note>, and half a pound of finely ground chalk—or in its place, sand, mica, or talc. Mix these well and work them into one another; the longer they are worked together, the better the mixture will be. Have a mold <term>a pattern or form</term> made of wood that you can take apart, secured with an iron ring and containing a core. With this, you can make the crucibles <term>heat-resistant melting pots</term> yourself, either large or small. When they are thoroughly dry, let them be fired well. These crucibles can withstand the heat for 48 hours; the thicker they are made, the longer they will last, and no metal will leak through them.

# Coelum Reseratum.

<margin>Chapter 14.</margin>
...cover [the apparatus] with wet cloths and secure the bung well. Plug it back up, but if you see that the <term>Spirits <note>original: "Spiritus"; in alchemy, these are the volatile vapors released during heating that condense into liquid.</note></term> are moving too forcefully, then open it again a little. Do this as often as you notice that the pressure threatens to blow off the **receivers** <note>the glass vessels at the ends of the tubes meant to collect the distillate</note>. When the reaction has ceased, pour in more fresh liquid, and continue this as long as the **Spirits** are flowing. When no more come over, then stop and let the **Spirits** settle for at least one day.

<margin>Spirit of Quicklime ☿ <note>The symbol ☿ refers to Mercury, signifying the volatile or "spirituous" part of the substance.</note></margin>
Then take the <term>Quicklime <note>original Latin: "Calcem vivam"; calcium oxide.</note></term> out of the basket and put fresh lime in again. Repeat this as often as necessary until you believe you have enough lye and **Spirit**. Afterward, pour even more water onto the **Quicklime**, and leach all the salt completely out of it. Let your salt solution evaporate <note>original German: "abrauchen"</note> until it reaches the consistency of a syrup.

Place this syrup into a flask and begin to <term>distill <note>the process of heating a liquid to create vapor and then cooling the vapor to collect the purified liquid.</note></term> in a <term>Water Bath <note>original Latin: "B. M." or Balneum Mariae; a vessel of hot water used to heat the flask gently and evenly.</note></term> until you notice that all the <term>Phlegm <note>original: "Phlegma"; the watery, inactive, or tasteless part of a distillate.</note></term> has come over. At that point, let the fire go out immediately. Place the flask in a sand bath and begin to **distill** again; a very pungent spirit will then come over. You must <term>rectify <note>original: "rectificiren"; to purify a liquid through repeated distillation.</note></term> this spirit at least twice more in total. Keep this well-stored in a cool place. Whatever remains behind in the flask should be placed into a <term>Retort <note>a glass vessel with a long, downward-pointing neck used for distilling substances that require higher heat.</note></term> and **distilled** very carefully <term>by degrees of fire <note>original Latin: "per gradus ignis"; a technique of slowly increasing the heat in stages.</note></term>.

<margin>The Soul of Lime; Hermetic Ambergris. ♃</margin>

coagulate it once more. Repeat this as often as necessary until it remains behind with the consistency of a **Butter** <note>in alchemy, "butter" refers to a substance with a thick, oily, or resinous consistency, such as "Butter of Antimony."</note>.
<margin>Spirit, Soul, and Body. Philosopher's Stone. See Chapter 49.</margin>
Thus you have the **Spirit**, **Soul**, and **Body**. You can use these to make the **Philosopher’s Stone** <note>original Latin: "Lapidem Philosophorum"; the legendary substance capable of turning base metals into gold and granting eternal life.</note>, as mentioned in the preceding chapters and their notes. Here you also have two paths to a **Tincture** <note>a powerful alchemical preparation used for transmutation or healing.</note>: first, when they are <term>fixed <note>original: "figiret"; the process of making a volatile substance stable under heat.</note></term> together; or second, 
<margin>Universal Solvent.</margin>
when a **Universal Solvent** <note>original Latin: "Menstruum Universale"; a liquid capable of dissolving all substances to their root components.</note> is made from it, which <term>radically dissolves <note>original: "radicaliter solviret"; to dissolve a substance completely down to its primary matter.</note></term> all metals. In short, this **Spirit** "opens and closes" all things <note>an alchemical metaphor: "opening" refers to dissolution (turning solid to liquid) and "closing" refers to coagulation (turning liquid to solid).</note>. These are the most noble and important works that a student must necessarily know. In these operations, many secret techniques are involved; if a student cannot help themselves in one work, they will find their errors in another. To our knowledge, there are no other works that function universally except for these prescribed operations, from which all **particular** <note>referring to "particular" transmutations, which only affect specific metals, as opposed to the "universal" work of the Stone.</note> works also derive.

## Key to the 1st Chapter

<margin>V. 10. 1.</margin>
That this little work is given only to our children <note>In alchemical literature, "children" or "Sons of Art" refers to initiated students or practitioners of alchemy rather than literal offspring</note> has its reasons; for if the <term>Manual Guidance</term> <note>original: "Manuduction," a practical handbook or instructional guide</note> is lost, no one can <term>accomplish</term> <note>original: "effectuiren"</note> anything without the <term>Keys</term> <note>original: "Claves"</note>, unless he achieves it through much labor. Whoever lacks the keys can do nothing at all; but the Lord, who holds everything in His hands, shall also protect this from those who are unworthy.

In the first chapter, the secret is to make the red flower flowing <note>original: "fließig," referring to making a substance fusible or capable of melting/flowing</note>. Grind that which was sublimated once more with the <term>residue</term>, and <term>sublimate</term> it yet again. Then, take all the <term>sublimate</term> together and leach <note>original: "ausgelauget," meaning to wash or extract soluble parts with a liquid</note> it, so that all the salt is removed from it,
